title: 14 Gift Ideas for Grandkids That Aren't Toys: Experiences to Share This Christmas
summary: Discover 14 meaningful gift ideas for grandkids that aren't toys, from baking and art classes to family outings and Christmas traditions they'll remember.
body_markdown:
The best gifts for grandkids this Christmas may not be on any Black Friday list. Ask a grown grandchild what they remember from the holidays, and it's rarely the toy. It's the afternoon baking cookies in your kitchen, the trip to the aquarium, the story the two of you made up on the couch. Those are the gifts that last, and none of them is sold out at the mall this week.


Here are 14 experience gifts for grandchildren, from a painting class to a "yes" day, with a note on the ones that need a ride. GoGoGrandparent arranges rides for older adults by phone, so if the gift is a trip to the zoo and you no longer drive, one call to1 (855) 464-6872 handles the getting there.


## **Why give an experience instead of a toy?**


Three reasons. A toy is opened once, while a tradition comes back every December. An experience puts you in the memory, which is the part a grandchild actually keeps. And an afternoon together asks for your time rather than your shopping stamina, which matters when the stores are loud and the parking lots are full. There's a bonus for you as well: a standing date with a grandchild is something to look forward to all month, and it sidesteps the annual guessing game about sizes, characters and whatever the cousins already own.


## **What are the best gift ideas for grandkids?**


### **1. Take an art class together**


Sign the two of you up for a painting or pottery class at a local studio or community center. Your grandkids get their hands messy, you get a keepsake with a date on the back, and nobody has to wrap anything. Community centers and libraries often schedule inexpensive weekend sessions in December specifically for grandparents and grandchildren, so ten minutes with your town's calendar is worth it. If the studio's across town, book a GoGo ride a day ahead and travel together, so the class starts in the car.


### **2. Explore nature on a guided walk**


A guided nature walk is a gift for the grandchild who collects rocks and asks about every bird. Pack a magnifying glass, a jar for bugs and a small field guide, and head to a local park or trail. Winter's better for this than it sounds: tracks in the snow, red birds against bare branches, animals getting ready for the cold. Take it at your own pace. Half the fun is stopping to see what they notice. A park entrance makes an easy pickup spot for the GoGo ride home.


### **3. Bake something in your kitchen**


A cooking day with Grandma or Grandpa is the whole gift for the little chef in the family. Holiday cookies, a snowman-shaped pizza, the family recipe nobody else knows how to make. They learn something, you pass something on, and everyone eats the results. If the heavy bags are the hard part, GoGo Grocery can bring the flour, butter and sprinkles to the door before they arrive, so you don't spend the morning of the big day in a checkout line. Same phone number, press 7 for delivery.


### **4. Make up a story together**


Instead of reading a book, write one. Invent the characters together, argue over the plot twist, and record it on a phone or write it down. Then type it up and have it printed as a small book. Years later it'll still be on a shelf, and it'll still be the two of you.


### **5. Visit the zoo or aquarium**


Nothing matches a child's face at the glass when the sea lion swims past. Many zoos and aquariums run behind-the-scenes tours and feeding times, which turn a visit into an event. Zoo parking is among the worst in any town, so let GoGo arrange the ride: call for the ride there, and call again when the penguins have been seen twice. You won't miss the sea lion show looking for a space.


### **6. Build a custom puzzle**


Several companies print a jigsaw from your own photo. Order one with the two of you on it, then spend a cozy afternoon putting your own faces back together. It's a gift and an activity in one, and you'll both want to finish it.


### **7. Plant a garden together**


A gardening kit with seeds, soil, and a child-sized pair of gloves is the gift that keeps going. Plant it together, then make each visit a check on how the beans are doing. A sunny windowsill works in December, and the real garden can wait for spring, when you'll both have something to check on every visit.


### **8. Host a movie marathon night**


Blankets on the floor, popcorn in the big bowl, their favorite holiday films, maybe a build-your-own-sundae bar. Let a different grandchild pick the movie each time and it becomes a tradition they'll ask for every year.


### **9. Give a craft subscription**


A monthly craft box arrives with a new project each time: friendship bracelets, a small robot, a birdhouse. It's one of the few gifts that keeps arriving all year, and it gives you something to ask about on every phone call. Subscriptions usually run three, six or twelve months, and the shorter one is a sensible way to discover whether your grandchild is a builder or a painter before you commit to a year of boxes.


### **10. Start a game night tradition**


Board games are where grandparents still win. Candy Land, Guess Who and Uno for the little ones; Ticket to Ride, Taboo or Scattergories once they are older. Ask the grandchild to explain the rules to you, which is excellent practice in patience for both generations. Our list of[intergenerational activities the whole family will love](https://www.gogograndparent.com/blog/15-intergenerational-activities-the-whole-family-will-love) has more ideas when the games run out.


### **11. Have a living room dance party**


Teach them your moves, let them teach you theirs, and make a playlist of every song you danced to. Send them home with it. Ten years from now, one of those songs will come on in a store and they'll think of you.


### **12. Make a memory scrapbook**


A scrapbooking kit, a shoebox of old photos, and an afternoon. They learn who the people in the pictures are, and you get to tell the stories. Photographs from your own childhood are especially popular, because a grandchild rarely believes you were ever seven. The finished book goes home with them, and the stories stay.


### **13. Plan a local adventure day**


The children's museum you have never been to, the science center, the playground on the other side of town. Spend one day being tourists in your own city. A GoGo ride takes the parking and the driving off your plate, so you can spend the energy on the grandkids instead of the traffic.


### **14. Give the gift of a "yes" day**


One day when the answer is yes, within reason. Ice cream for breakfast, a fort in the living room, the park twice. If the day involves an outing, book the GoGo ride and let them pick the destination. It's their day, after all.


## **What about grandchildren who live far away?**


The experiences above still work with a little planning, and in our experience consistency matters more than scale: a ten-minute weekly call about the craft box beats an elaborate visit that happens once. Mail the craft kit and do it together on a video call. Make the story over the phone, a chapter a week. Order the custom puzzle to their house and race to finish your copy first. And when a visit is possible, a trip to see them is the gift: GoGo arranges rides for older adults by phone, including the trip to the airport or the train, with a highly rated driver and the GoGo Guardians team able to monitor the ride. The[rides for seniors](https://www.gogograndparent.com/services/rides-for-seniors) page shows how a booking works.


## **Which gift lasts the longest?**


The magic of Christmas was never under the tree. This year, give the afternoon, the trip or the tradition, and skip the line at the store. The grandkids won't remember what the toy cost, but they'll remember who baked with them. ## **FAQ**


### **What is a good gift for grandchildren that isn't a toy?**


An experience you share: a class, a day out, a baking afternoon, a story you write together, or a tradition like a monthly movie night. Any of the 14 ideas above fits a different age and budget.


### **What can I give grandchildren who live far away?**


A craft kit you do together on a video call, a story written a chapter at a time over the phone, a custom puzzle mailed to both houses, or the visit itself. A ride to the airport or the train station can be scheduled by phone, with a call for the ride home when you're ready.


### **How can a grandparent who no longer drives get to these outings?**


Call1 (855) 464-6872 and schedule the ride there, then call again when you're ready to be picked up. If a grandchild is riding along, bring your own car seat or booster, the same as in any car; the driver does not provide one. No smartphone or app is needed, and a family member can arrange it once they've been added to the account.


### **Are experience gifts good for younger grandchildren?**


Yes, with the age in mind. A baking day, a movie night and a "yes" day work from about age four. Classes, custom puzzles and the story book suit school-age children. The dance party and the game night work at any age, including yours.
